newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Iran sees regional stability with Russian help.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees regional stability with Russian help.

text.p: Iranian President Ali Akbar Rafsanjani said on Saturday Iran was ready to cooperate with Russia to restore stability in Tajikistan and end a civil war in neighbouring Afghanistan.
"Iran and Russia share a common goal, including the settlement of the Tajik conflict," Rafsanjani told a news conference in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
He said Iran would develop cooperation with Russia further, including in the extraction of oil and gas.
"Our cooperation (with Russia) will play a great role in settling conflicts in Afghanistan and Tajikistan," he said.
Iran and Russia are guaranteeing the implementation of a ceasefire reached last December between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov's secular government and the Islamist opposition.
Rakhmonov called on Iran to invest in Tajik roads, transport and communications, including helping to upgrade the Tursunzade aluminium plant.
Investment projects include a $28 million road to be built over the next three years to link the south and the east of mountainous Tajikistan.
But Rafsanjani said: "As long as there is no peace, stability and national accord, one can't invest big money here."
The fragile peace in the former Soviet republic is often disturbed by armed bands and drug traffickers, many of them operating from Afghanistan.
Russia has nearly 20,000 troops in Tajikistan and it views the force as a shield against the possible incursion of militant Islam from Afghanistan.
Iran, itself an Islamic republic, has repeatedly criticised Afghan's Taleban militia for its extreme views of Islam.
Tajikistan, like Central Asia's other republics, fears that the Taleban may launch a summer offensive to gain control of northern Afghan territory.
Rakhmonov recently said he feared up to a million refugees could flood his country from Afghanistan if hostilities resumed.
Rakhmonov and Rafsanjani are waiting for the arrival of ousted Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani -- driven out of Kabul last September -- to discuss regional security issues.
A meeting of the three presidents, originally scheduled for Friday, is now likely to take place later on Saturday.
